title: The Small-Set Expansion Hypothesis
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: For every constant η>0, does there exist δ>0 such that it is NP-hard to distinguish a regular graph containing a set of δ times its vertices with normalized edge expansion at most η from one in which every such set has expansion at least 1−η?
context:
The small-set size and gap are fixed before the input graph; property testing of expansion is a different problem.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: A major proposed basis for hardness of graph partitioning and layout problems, with connections to Unique Games.
